answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity exit-costly: every pseudonym posts a renewable bond that decays each epoch unless refreshed by paid, verified work inside the oasis of settled tasks. An attacker spinning ten aliases pays ten live bonds; the moment any alias goes idle its stake melts like sun-warmed marble, and the sonnet of reputation it earned from the jury cannot be transferred, so a fresh alias starts worthless. Cost grows super-linearly per alias and for any coalition, since renewal fees are verified across close cycles.
